tests.notes: * binds tighter than +, so a + b * c is a + (b * c)
*, / and % share a level and group left to right; with truncating division the grouping changes the result (7 / 2 * 2 == 6)
compiles successfully; + and - group left to right; subThenAdd(1, 3, 5) reverts with Panic(0x11) at the first subtraction
** binds tighter than *, so a * b ** c is a * (b ** c)
in Solidity -a ** b is (-a) ** b, the opposite of ordinary mathematical convention; -2 ** 2 evaluates to 4
<< and >> bind looser than + and -, so a << b + c is a << (b + c)
shifts group left to right: a << b >> c is (a << b) >> c
&, ^ and | are three separate levels, tightest to loosest, so a | b ^ c & d is a | (b ^ (c & d))
arithmetic binds tighter than relational and equality operators
unlike C, bitwise operators bind tighter than relational and equality in Solidity; x & mask == expected is (x & mask) == expected and compiles without parentheses
a < b == c < d is (a < b) == (c < d)
comparisons bind tighter than && and ||, and && tighter than ||
a || b ? x : y is (a || b) ? x : y
a = b = c is a = (b = c); the inner assignment evaluates to the assigned value and may be implicitly widened
assignment has the lowest precedence; x *= a + b is x = x * (a + b)
indexing and member access bind tighter than unary operators: -arr[i] negates the element, !s.ok negates the field
prefix ~, ! and - bind tighter than every binary operator: ~a & b is (~a) & b
an explicit conversion binds tighter than binary operators: uint8(x) + y truncates x first, uint8(x + y) truncates after adding
one expression across six precedence levels (**, *, +, <<, &, |); implicit and explicit forms must agree
unary plus does not exist in Solidity (removed in 0.5.0)
unary minus binds tighter than **, so -a ** b negates an unsigned a first, which is invalid
++ and -- need an lvalue; (a + b) is a temporary value
assignment is lowest precedence, so a + b = c groups as (a + b) = c, assigning to a temporary
a == b == c is (a == b) == c, comparing a bool with an integer; not an all-three-equal check
